name: Deborah K. Ross
office: U.S. House, North Carolina 2nd Congressional District, 2026
profileSummary: Three-term progressive congresswoman and former NC-ACLU director with near-perfect environmental and gun safety records; champions public transit investment, prescription drug price reform, and police accountability from a reform-oriented but establishment-aligned posture.
keyPositions: LCV 100% (2024), 99% lifetime -- near-perfect environmental voting record; authored IRA offshore wind provision
Supports public option and ACA expansion, explicitly not Medicare for All; authored PBM Reform Act (passed House Jan 2026)
Voted for assault weapons ban and Bipartisan Safer Communities Act; endorsed by Brady PAC and Everytown
Co-sponsored George Floyd Justice in Policing Act; former NC-ACLU director who pioneered anti-racial profiling legislation
Voted for ARP, Infrastructure Act, CHIPS Act, and IRA -- consistent support for major public investment

climate_permitting.notes: Nuanced position: wants faster permitting specifically for clean energy, while maintaining or strengthening environmental review for fossil fuels. She is not a blanket deregulator on permitting -- she wants to selectively accelerate green projects. This is faster green permitting (toward Pole B direction) but with maintained environmental review for fossil projects, placing her at 3 rather than 0 or 5.

universalism.reasoning: Environmental protection is central (LCV 99% lifetime). Racial justice advocacy spans 30 years (ACLU directorship, anti-profiling bills, George Floyd Act). Reproductive rights champion. Safety net expansion for all. Housing fairness. Consistent concern for welfare of all people and nature across career. Not scored at 1.0 because some positions are pragmatic center-left (public option not M4A) rather than maximally universalist.

benevolence.reasoning: Worker protections (Raise the Wage Act), community investment (transit, broadband, affordable housing), healthcare access expansion, youth offender rehabilitation. Strong care-for-community orientation. Her legislative focus on Wake County constituents (transit, broadband, housing) shows in-group care. Slightly below universalism because her focus extends broadly beyond in-group to systemic concerns.

self_direction.reasoning: First Amendment advocacy from ACLU career. Independent positioning (public option rather than following progressive base on M4A). Civil liberties orientation throughout career. But governance approach is predominantly collective and regulatory -- she favors government-led solutions, which works against pure individual autonomy as a value.

achievement.reasoning: Notable legislative productivity: authored successful bills (PBM Reform Act passed House, IRA offshore wind provision enacted), secured significant funding ($176M+ NC transit). Career trajectory from ACLU director to state legislator to congresswoman to Chief Deputy Whip shows competence-driven advancement. But achievement serves policy goals rather than being an end in itself.

stimulation.reasoning: Embraces new energy technologies (offshore wind, battery storage, grid modernization). Introduced innovative policy approaches (prison gerrymandering reform, PBM structural reform). But overall style is pragmatic establishment rather than revolutionary or risk-seeking. Innovation serves established progressive goals.

security.reasoning: Gun safety framing is partially about community security. Public health orientation includes protective elements. But consistently prioritizes reform and civil liberties over security concerns -- challenges police authority, opposes security-maximalist approaches. The net signal is near-neutral with a very slight positive from the community safety dimension of gun regulation.

conformity.reasoning: Actively challenges existing legal structures: qualified immunity reform, racial profiling law changes, prison gerrymandering reform, new energy regulatory frameworks. ACLU career is fundamentally about challenging government authority and established rules when they conflict with rights. Chief Deputy Whip role shows institutional participation, but her policy agenda consistently pushes to change rather than uphold existing rules.

tradition.reasoning: Progressive reformer throughout career. Pushes for structural changes in energy systems (away from fossil fuels), policing models (away from status quo), tax structures (away from current distribution), and criminal justice (away from punitive norms). Career defined by changing established systems rather than preserving them. No traditional/conservative cultural appeals found in campaign materials.

power.reasoning: Policy orientation is redistributive: from high earners to safety net, from institutional investors to everyday homeowners, from police authority to civilian oversight. Opposes concentrated economic power (PBM reform, institutional investor accountability). Holds institutional leadership (Chief Deputy Whip) but uses it for redistributive rather than power-concentrating ends.

hedonism.reasoning: No meaningful evidence in either direction. Campaign and legislative record are policy-focused without hedonistic or anti-hedonistic themes.

conflicts.topic: Healthcare coverage model: public option vs. Medicare for All
conflicts.description: NC Medicare for All Coalition has urged Ross to cosponsor the Medicare for All Act; she has not done so. She explicitly supports a public option and ACA expansion, not single-payer. This is not a conflict between stated and actual positions -- it is a known gap between progressive base expectations and her actual policy position.
